The bug in the middleware's GetHead handler is that it does not properly handle HEAD requests when no explicit HEAD route exists. It falls back to a GET request but then returns whatever body was written by the GET handler, which violates HTTP semantics for HEAD (the response body must be empty). The fix adds logic: after falling back to a GET and calling next.ServeHTTP, it explicitly writes an empty response with only headers (`w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)`), ensuring no body is sent. The bug in `GetHead` was a logical error in the condition checking the request method. The original code used `if r.Method != "HEAD"`, which incorrectly short-circuited HEAD requests and prevented proper handling of HEAD routes. The fix is to change this condition to `if r.Method == "HEAD"`. After applying the replacement, re-running the test suite confirms that `TestGetHead` now passes without modifying any tests.
